title: Changing state and the water cycle

steps.say: Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas. Water can be all three: ice, water and water vapour.

figure.alt: Ice as a solid, water as a liquid and water vapour as a gas.

steps.say: Ice melts at 0 °C. Water boils at 100 °C.
Water can also evaporate below 100 °C. That is how puddles and wet clothes dry.
When water vapour cools, it condenses back into liquid water. That is how drops form on a cold glass.
In the water cycle, the Sun heats the sea and water evaporates. The water vapour rises, cools and condenses into clouds.

figure.alt: The water cycle: water evaporates from the sea, condenses into clouds, falls as rain and flows back in rivers.

steps.say: Rain falls and flows in rivers back to the sea. Then the cycle starts again.

check.prompt: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns into liquid water?

options.why: Evaporating turns a liquid into a gas, the opposite change.
Melting turns a solid into a liquid.
Freezing turns a liquid into a solid.

hints: This change goes from a gas to a liquid.
It happens on a cold glass or a cold window.
Cross out the changes that start with a solid or a liquid.
check.explanation: Condensing is the change from a gas to a liquid. Water vapour condenses when it cools.

check.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
hints: Boiling is when water bubbles and turns into a gas quickly.
It is much hotter than a hot bath.
Think of the water in a kettle when it starts to bubble hard.
check.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C at sea level and freezes at 0 °C.
